body.claim: A symbol path is what makes an anchor durable: across five corpora, every record that detached immediately after import was one with no symbol.
body.detail: Verifying a freshly imported corpus against the very code it came from should resolve everything. Java 0 and Go 0 detached; Rust 22 of 27,642 (0.08%), C++ 17 of 5,261 (0.32%), TypeScript 71 of 4,147 (1.71%) — and in all five, every single one carried no symbol. Without a symbol an anchor can only match by content, so two constructs with identical bodies are indistinguishable and ambiguity is failure rather than a tiebreak. This is the measured justification for the symbol path, and for treating a language adapter that fails to name a declaration form as a correctness problem rather than a cosmetic one.
